Anika: Pushed the int8 per-channel quantized vectors for cormorant-lite to staging and ran the usual recall/cluster suite. Seeing a pretty consistent drop on short queries (<= 6 tokens). float32 recall@10: 0.872 -> int8-perchannel: 0.810. silhouette score dropped 0.42 -> 0.33. Anyone seen this pattern before?
Ryan: How big is the calibration set you used? and seed for the eval?
Anika: Calibration set was 5k random docs from wiki-anchors-10k (seen in config). eval seed 42. k=10, metric=recall@k, queries are short-heavy (median tokens=4). Config snippet:
```
runner: eval_embeddings
dataset: wiki-anchors-10k
calib_set: wiki-anchors-5k
quant: int8_perchannel
normalize: l2
seed: 42
```
Sam: Short queries amplify small per-dim scaling errors — per-channel scaling can skew directionality for small norm vectors. Did you check pre/post-normalization norms?
Anika: Good point. Pre-normalize L2 means quantization happens on pre-normalized floats. I compared norms: avg norm pre-quant ~1.02, post-dequant ~0.98, but variance increased.
Lena: Two quick experiments: 1) run int8-pertensor symmetric quant with calibration to see if variance drops. 2) try re-normalize after dequant (i.e., dequant -> l2 normalize). For many pipelines we do dequant+normalize to recover direction.
Anika: Ran 1) and 2). Results: pertensor symmetric recall@10: 0.838 (better), dequant+normalize on perchannel: 0.829 (improvement but still below float).
Ryan: Can you paste the cluster shift numbers? e.g., centroid cosine before/after for a couple anchors.
Anika: Sure — sample anchor cluster "cryptography":
- float centroid cos->cluster members mean: 0.87
- int8-perchannel centroid->members mean: 0.78
- after dequant+normalize: 0.81
Also noticed more id-flips near cluster boundaries.
Sam: Sounds like quantization noise is anisotropic across dims. Consider per-dim bias correction using calibration stats: collect per-dim mean and stdev on calib set and apply a small affine correction prior to quantize (shift + scale). We've used that to reduce centroid shift on other models.
Lena: Another small thing: check embedding whitening/PC projection in the pipeline. If your clustering relies on a whitening fitted on float vectors, quantization can change PC directions. Try refitting PCA on quantized vectors or apply the same transform post-dequant.
Anika: Filing quick experiment list: 
- run pertensor symmetric quant baseline (done)
- run perchannel + dequant+re-normalize + pca-refit (queued)
- per-dim bias correction on calib set (queued)
- eval with longer-query subset to confirm it's short-query specific (queued)

eval-bot: job 321789 queued: embed-eval/6161712345/321789 — will post results when done.
Ryan: For the per-dim correction, watch for overfitting to calibration set. Use k-fold calib or holdout. Also compare recall@1/5/10 to see where most regressions occur.
Anika: Will do k-fold calib (3 folds) and post numbers. Also tagging the internal note: <https://redwood.internal/embeddings/quant-calib-hacks> for checklist.
Sam: If per-dim helps, we can bake it into Optimize as a suggested post-quant step for short-query workloads.
Lena: Nice. If folks are free later we can pair on the PCA/refit step — I think that'll tell us if directionality change is the primary issue. :thinking_face:
Anika: Thanks all — will update here with job output. :party_parrot:
